claims.text: Cryo-rolling followed by non-isothermal annealing can simultaneously enhance yield strength and tensile ductility in a brittle multiphase MPEA.
The proposed processing route produces a two-hierarchical heterogeneous microstructure combining ultrafine lamellar and coarse non-lamellar regions.
The as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a coarse lamellar morphology.
The as-cast alloy is brittle at room temperature because of limited dislocation mobility and insufficient strain-hardening capacity.
The alloy can be cryo-rolled by multiple passes to approximately 90% thickness reduction, with liquid-nitrogen immersion before and after each pass.
The cryo-rolled alloy should then be non-isothermally annealed at 660–900 °C for 1 hour using a 10 °C/min heating rate and water quenching.
Cryo-rolling should be maintained below -180 °C and annealing should be performed under argon.
The fine lamellar regions contain dual-phase FCC/B2 grains approximately 0.5–1 µm in size.
The coarse non-lamellar regions contain unrecrystallized B2 grains approximately 2–3 µm in size.
The fine and coarse regions create domain boundaries with substantial hardness contrast and strain gradients.
Hardness contrast between soft FCC and hard B2 domains generates geometrically necessary dislocations and long-range back stress at domain boundaries.
Back-stress strengthening contributes approximately 950 MPa to the strength.
Strain-gradient hardening in the heterogeneous structure distributes plastic deformation and delays necking.
Ductile phases arrest microcracks and thereby help retain or enhance tensile ductility.
The proposed treatment is expected to produce a yield strength of approximately 1.4–1.5 GPa and elongation to failure of approximately 14–16%.
These properties represent simultaneous strength and ductility enhancement rather than the conventional strength–ductility trade-off.
Cold rolling without cryogenic treatment or conventional annealing produces homogeneous microstructures that fail to enhance strength and ductility simultaneously.
The strategy is applicable to multiphase FCC/B2 or FCC/BCC MPEAs with moderate stacking-fault energy.
The strategy may be less effective in single-phase alloys or alloys with extremely high or low stacking-fault energy because their twinning and slip mechanisms differ.
Over-annealing may coarsen the grains and reduce strength.

contradictions.description: The baseline broadly states that cold rolling without cryogenic treatment cannot simultaneously enhance strength and ductility, whereas cited record node::W2911870840 reports about 1.5 GPa yield strength and about 16% elongation after conventional multi-pass cold rolling and non-isothermal annealing of the same AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy.

The initial material is described as room-temperature brittle, but the predicted 14–16% elongation is said to be maintained or improved; cited record node::W2788103315 reports about 14% elongation remaining almost unchanged from the as-cast material, creating tension with the characterization of the initial state as brittle.
